title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 44 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 44)

content.overview: Section 44 defines a foreign award for Chapter I of Part II. It requires an arbitral award on differences arising from legal relationships, contractual or otherwise, treated as commercial under Indian law, made on or after 11 October 1960, pursuant to a written arbitration agreement to which the New York Convention applies and in a notified reciprocating territory.

content.study:
Section 44 — Definition of foreign award

Section 44 defines a foreign award for Chapter I of Part II. It requires an arbitral award on differences arising from legal relationships, contractual or otherwise, treated as commercial under Indian law, made on or after 11 October 1960, pursuant to a written arbitration agreement to which the New York Convention applies and in a notified reciprocating territory.

The Part II analysis must begin with the statutory definition and the Convention framework, then identify the exact condition or enforcement ground engaged. The statutory grounds should not be expanded by general merits review.
